fixture: by-links-3d, a 3D default layout: each case's input and the answer the reference implementation gives
call: the layout of the graph { nodes: input.nodes, edges: input.edges } with input.rows as the world's elements, at `steps` force steps (300, the method's own count, in every case); input.held and input.heldUnit are handed only where the input has the key (a null is handed as null)
rows: input.rows is the world's Map and Pin elements as served (only the keys the map-space profile and its layout reading read), or null. They are read as the map-space profile reads them, and its layout reading says which Map is a layout map; the method has no reading of its own
table: table_sha256 is the sha256 of the directions table the method reads (directions.json), the same bytes in every implementation

compare.exact: every element whose how is centre, with or map: each of x, y, z the same double, a zero compared by its value whatever its sign, because the file's JSON holds no -0 (JSON writes -0 as 0); and every how, group, part, held, centres and ids entry
compare.within: every element whose how is arm, link or shelf and whose held is false: each of x, y, z within 1e-9 of a rest (6e-8 units), because those are placed with the runtime's cosine and sine
compare.held: every element whose want.held is true, whatever its how: each of x, y, z the same double as input.held gives for it (it stands at its held point)
compare.refused: a case whose want is { refused: code }: the call throws before anything runs, and the error carries that code (in JavaScript err.code, on a TypeError for held-not-object and held-not-point, a RangeError for held-box and held-unit)
compare.unplaced: exact: the same ids in the same order

held: a case named "held: ..." hands back points the method answered for an earlier input (input.held, element id to [x, y, z]; with input.heldUnit where the points were rounded)
points: want.points is x, y, z of each element in want.ids order (the order input.nodes was handed in), 3 numbers an element
unplaced: `unplaced`, after the cases: for each case, the id of every node of graph.nodes that is not in placed, in code point order (the method places every node it is handed). A member of placed that is not a non-empty string is passed over; a placed id that is no node is no part of the answer
